# c-parse-kv

`kv_parse_line` accepts a line whose value is exactly 64 characters long (`KV_VALUE_MAX`) instead of rejecting it, and the sanitizer build of the test aborts with an AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow` WRITE inside `kv_parse_line` on that input. Values up to 63 characters parse correctly. Per `kv.h`, both fields must stay NUL-terminated inside their fixed-size buffers. Fix `kv.c`; do not modify `held_out_test_kv.c`.


Task: fix this bug in the attached repository. Start by reading the relevant source file with read_file, then change it with edit_file (exact old text -> new text; the user reviews it as a diff), then verify by running the project's build and test commands with run_command (build: ["clang", "-fsanitize=address,undefined", "-Wall", "-Werror", "kv.c", "held_out_test_kv.c", "-o", "held_out_test_kv"]; test: ["./held_out_test_kv"]). Do not modify the test files. When the test passes, summarize what you changed.

The bug is in `kv_parse_line`: it does not check if the value length exceeds `KV_VALUE_MAX` (64 characters) before copying. The current check `value_len > sizeof out->value` is incorrect because `sizeof out->value` is 65 (64 + 1 for the NUL terminator), but the function should reject values longer than 64 characters.

I will fix this by adding a check for `value_len > KV_VALUE_MAX` (64) before copying the value.

Let me propose the edit.
